findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-100 — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a zod **SafeParseReturn** (`{success, data}`), not the parsed key, and it is written straight to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the plain object. Every Google refresh now persists `{"success":true,"data":{…}}` as `Credential.key`, bricking the integration on first refresh. The other two call sites (office365calendar:264, salesforce:92-98) unwrap `.data` — the helper contract was applied inconsistently.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma.credential.update` is called but `prisma` is never imported (verified: imports end at `parseRefreshTokenResponse`). Compile failure / `ReferenceError` on every Salesforce client construction.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11 — `minimumTokenResponseSchema`'s computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both stringify to the same literal (`"[object Object]"`), so the second overwrites the first. The "any numeric property is the expiry" and "allow other properties" behavior the comments promise does not exist; the schema is effectively `{access_token: string}` and, being a default stripping `z.object`, **discards every other field** (`refresh_token`, `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `instance_url`, `scope`). In sync mode the stripped object is persisted, destroying the credential while reporting success — a textbook silent-pass gate. Needs `.passthrough()`/`.catchall()`.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 — In sync mode the helper returns a raw `fetch` `Response`; otherwise it returns whatever the per-app `refreshFunction` yields (Gaxios response for Google, parsed `HubspotToken` for HubSpot, `Response` for lark/office365/webex). No caller handles both. Google reads `res?.data` → `undefined` → `token.access_token` throws; HubSpot computes `expiryDate` from `undefined` → `NaN` and persists a `Response` object as the credential key. The `refreshFunction: () => any` signature erases the types that would have caught this. The core feature of the PR does not work for Google or HubSpot.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-59 — The `state.teamId` branch creates a team-wide credential after only checking `members.some({userId, accepted: true})` — any accepted member, including a plain MEMBER, can install or overwrite org-wide OAuth credentials. `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` sits on the branch reached only when `state?.teamId` is falsy, so it is always invoked with `teamId: null` and is structurally dead. The authorization gate is effectively inverted. (`members: { select: { userId } }` is also selected and never read.)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — `req.headers[name] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` **fails open**: with the secret unset and the header absent, `undefined !== undefined` is false and auth passes. The handler then writes arbitrary `key` JSON to any `userId`'s credential row — unauthenticated account/calendar takeover on a deployment where sharing is on but the secret was forgotten. Needs an explicit "secret is configured" assertion plus length-checked `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:24-26 — When the response lacks a refresh token, the code assigns the **literal string** `"refresh_token"` and callers persist it. Combined with #3 (which strips `refresh_token` out of `data`), this fires on essentially every sync-mode refresh, so credentials end up with a garbage refresh token. In office365calendar the spread overwrites a previously *valid* stored token. Subsequent refreshes fail at the provider with `invalid_grant`, far from the cause, and nothing recognizes the sentinel as a placeholder.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99 — The new refresh runs unconditionally on **every** `getClient()` — no expiry check — issuing a `login.salesforce.com` round-trip plus a `credential.update` per booking/availability call. Self-inflicted rate limiting, DB write amplification, and concurrent constructions race on the same row (last writer wins, one access token silently invalidated). It also calls `fetch` directly instead of `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce silently opts out of the very credential-sync feature this PR adds — while still validating with the sync schema. And the freshly persisted token is discarded: the returned `jsforce.Connection` is built from the stale `credentialKey.access_token`.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText})` — `statusText` is empty over HTTP/2 and unguaranteed under undici, so successful refreshes throw a 400 with an empty message; conversely a proxy sending `"OK"` with a non-200 passes. Use `!response.ok`, and include the response body in the error.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — The sync `fetch` has **no timeout/abort signal**, no `response.ok` check, and no retry. Node fetch has no default timeout, so a hanging self-hosted endpoint blocks token refresh on the booking/availability hot path indefinitely, for every user of every OAuth app. A 4xx/5xx or HTML error page is returned as if it were a token response.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — The outbound leg carries **no authentication** — only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, no shared secret or signature — while the inbound webhook is secret-protected. There is no scheme validation either, so an `http://` endpoint ships the token exchange in cleartext. Anyone who can reach or spoof that endpoint obtains access tokens for an arbitrary user id.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59 — The decrypted `keys` is `JSON.parse` output typed `any`, written to `credential.key` with **zero schema validation**. A caller with the secret can persist `"hello"` or `null` as any app's credential; consuming `CalendarService`s then crash at use time rather than at write time. `symmetricDecrypt(..., process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY \

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31, 57-59 — No try/catch anywhere: `schema.parse` (not `safeParse`) throws `ZodError` on a malformed body, and `symmetricDecrypt` + `JSON.parse` throw on a bad key or non-JSON plaintext. All surface as unhandled 500s with stack detail instead of the `{message}` JSON shape every other branch returns — and a caller's retry loop cannot distinguish a permanently-bad payload from a transient outage, so it retries forever.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:176-201 — HubSpot is the one migrated app that never calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, and it asserts the helper's return as `HubspotToken`. In sync mode it writes a serialized `Response`/`NaN` expiry to `credential.key` and calls `setAccessToken(undefined)`; the only handler is `this.log.error(e)`, so the credential is left in a worse state than before with no user-visible failure.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262-264 — Behavior changed from log-and-continue to throw: `safeParse` became `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (which throws), so the surviving `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` spread guard is dead, and the diff **deleted the only diagnostic** (`console.error` with the zod error and the raw MS response). In sync mode `data` is only `{access_token}`, so the spread leaves the stale `expires_in`/`refresh_token` in place — the credential looks refreshed but the expiry never advances, producing a refresh-on-every-call loop.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:19-21 — All failures collapse into a generic `throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` with the zod error and raw response discarded — across ~7 integrations, with no app name attached. Combined with #15's deleted logging, refresh failures become effectively undebuggable for operators.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92-94 — `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) return Promise.reject(...)` is unreachable — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure and only ever returns a success result. The intended graceful rejection never runs, and the dead branch misrepresents the helper's contract to future readers.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:5-11`, `encodeOAuthState.ts:5-11 — OAuth `state` is unsigned, unencoded, and unbound to the session. `encodeOAuthState` is an identity function (parse→stringify) adding no CSRF token, HMAC, or session binding, despite a name implying protection; `decodeOAuthState` then trusts `teamId`/`returnTo` from a fully attacker-controlled callback URL, passing `teamId` straight into a Prisma `where` with no type check. The only thing preventing cross-tenant credential planting is the (already weak) membership query in #5.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-90 — `findFirst` → `create`/`update` is a check-then-act TOCTOU with no transaction and no unique constraint on `(userId, appId)`. Two concurrent syncs (trivially triggered by a retrying caller) both insert; later `findFirst` consumers then non-deterministically pick one, so some bookings use a stale credential.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:16-17 — No HTTP method guard — `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE` reach the credential mutation path identically to `POST`. Sibling routes in this same diff (e.g. `zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:11`) do check `req.method`. The absence of the codebase's `defaultHandler`/`defaultResponder` is also why the error handling in #13 is missing.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — Secret comparison uses `!==`, which is non-constant-time, on an endpoint with no rate limiting — a byte-at-a-time oracle in principle, and an unbounded brute-force surface in practice.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:65-77 — The update path does not clear an `invalid` flag or reconcile `type` (only the create path sets it). A previously-invalidated credential stays invalid, and drifted types are never corrected, while the caller gets a 200 "Credentials updated" and the integration remains broken.
`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` (whole file)

.env.example:233-243` + `refreshOAuthTokens.ts:4`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:14`, `app-credential.ts:20 — The enablement predicate `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is duplicated verbatim in two files while the webhook checks only `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`, so three call sites can disagree about whether the feature is on. New env vars are read raw from `process.env` rather than via the constants module. The comment block also contradicts itself: "must be 32 bytes for AES256" alongside `openssl rand -base64 24`.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:57 — `this.conn = this.getClient(credential).then(...)` in the constructor now performs network I/O that can reject. Constructing the service without immediately awaiting `this.conn` produces an unhandled promise rejection — fatal in Node 15+ under default settings. Previously `getClient` was effectively synchronous.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9`, `encodeOAuthState.ts:9 — `JSON.parse(req.query.state)` is unguarded in both, and the result is cast to `IntegrationOAuthCallbackState` without validation. A tampered or truncated `state` throws inside every `add`/`callback` handler and inside `createOAuthAppCredential`, yielding a 500 mid-install instead of a redirect to the error page. Content is carried over from the pre-move files, so the defect is pre-existing — but the move is a cheap opportunity to wrap it.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-59 — Two different authorization rules (any-accepted-member vs. admin-access) now live in one function, with the team branch hand-rolling its own check instead of reusing the helper. Structural cause of #5; worth fixing as one gate.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:37-56 — `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: {slug}, select: {slug} })` returns exactly the slug already in the request body, and `app.slug` is used only to index `appStoreMetadata` — a DB round-trip establishing nothing the metadata lookup doesn't, followed by two near-identical "App not found" responses.

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — `appConfig.slug` replaced with the hardcoded literal `"zoho-bigin"` in the redirect URI while `appConfig` is still used on lines 12 and 22. Unrelated to the PR intent and reintroduces drift between the key lookup and the registered OAuth redirect URI.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — `req.headers[name] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` **fails open**: with the secret unset and the header absent, `undefined !== undefined` is false and auth passes. packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:24-26 — When the response lacks a refresh token, the code assigns the **literal string** `"refresh_token"` and callers persist it. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99 — The new refresh runs unconditionally on **every** `getClient()` — no expiry check — issuing a `login.salesforce.com` round-trip plus a `credential.update` per booking/availability call. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText})` — `statusText` is empty over HTTP/2 and unguaranteed under undici, so successful refreshes throw a 400 with an empty message; conversely a proxy sending `"OK"` with a non-200 passes. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — The sync `fetch` has **no timeout/abort signal**, no `response.ok` check, and no retry. Since Node/undici `fetch` has no default timeout, this call can hang indefinitely if the self-hosted endpoint stalls, and non-2xx responses (including HTML error pages) are passed upstream as if they were successful token-refresh responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59 — The decrypted `keys` is `JSON.parse` output typed `any`, written to `credential.key` with **zero schema validation**. A caller with the secret can persist `"hello"` or `null` as any app's credential; consuming `CalendarService`s then crash at use time rather than at write time. `symmetricDecrypt(..., process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY \

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the code decrypts `reqBody.keys` and immediately does `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`, then writes `key: keys` into `prisma.credential.update/create` without validating the decrypted JSON against any app-specific schema. Since `keys` is effectively `any`, a caller who knows the webhook secret can send encrypted JSON such as `"hello"` (a JSON string) or `null`, which will successfully `JSON.parse` and be persisted. adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-90 — `findFirst` → `create`/`update` is a check-then-act TOCTOU with no transaction and no unique constraint on `(userId, appId)`. adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler does a non-atomic “check then act”: it calls `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and then, based on the result, either `credential.update` or `credential.create`.
